applicability: Any two positive real numbers a and b: a% of b equals b% of a. Pick whichever side is easier to compute.

steps.instruction: Flip: a% of b = b% of a

assignment.note: The two draws are used as the percent (a=7) and the base (b=20). The pose 'a% of b' is the awkward direction; the swap 'b% of a' turns 20% into one fifth, which is trivial to divide 7 by.

universality_evidence.claim: For all a, b in this domain, (a/100) * b == (b/100) * a as exact rationals.
universality_evidence.note: The identity is commutativity of multiplication on rationals; no whitelisted theorem in core/verify/theorems.json covers it directly, so §3.2 is satisfied by exhaustive symbolic check over the stated finite domain.

nulls.reason: The rule a% of b = b% of a is (a/100)*b = (b/100)*a, i.e. commutativity of multiplication on the reals. There is no input in the stated applicability where the equality fails; the generator check performs an exhaustive symbolic sweep to confirm.
